grades_v0.reason: The chain has a supported element-localization step but no direct support for TCF7L2 allele-specific binding, for MYC regulation by this element/variant, or for the direction alt C > TCF7L2 > MYC. TCF7L2 appears chosen without QBiC-SELEX, motif, ChIP, or perturbation evidence.
E03 directly places the variant in cCRE EH38E3858447, a pELS; E01 also annotates a regulatory enhancer. This supports the element-localization claim.

E02 shows MYC is 334.2 kb upstream, and E06 contains general 8q24/MYC colorectal cancer literature, but no cited evidence shows this cCRE/variant regulates MYC or that this element is in a validated MYC regulatory interaction.
E06 is a keyword literature list with some colorectal cancer context, but it does not establish TCF7L2 expression, TCF7L2 binding, or this mechanism in HCT 116.

E06 supports general MYC/8q24 colorectal cancer relevance, but not that increased MYC caused by this variant is the disease mechanism. No perturbation or genetic evidence ties rs73706717 to MYC or CRC.

E03 shows CTCF ChIP signal at the containing cCRE, but the values are maxima across ENCODE biosamples, not HCT 116, and are not allele-specific. No QBiC-SELEX row or other evidence shows alt C binds CTCF more than ref T. This is at best occupancy context, not allele-specific binding.
E01/E03 support that the variant lies in a pELS with CTCF signal, but they do not show that altered CTCF occupancy changes enhancer or insulator behavior at this element.

E02 supports POU5F1B as the closest protein-coding gene and that the variant is in its gene body. E05 does show best L2G POU5F1B 0.83, but the credible sets are PSA and urinary incontinence, not colorectal cancer, with PIP 0.04. E06 gives general POU5F1B colon cancer literature. No chromatin interaction or allele-specific regulatory assay links this element to POU5F1B.
E06 provides POU5F1B colorectal cancer literature, but not evidence for this variant, this element, or HCT 116 specifically.
E06 PMID 42465001 links POU5F1B to colon cancer cell growth/invasion, supporting general disease relevance, but not a causal rs73706717 effect. E05 is non-CRC disease evidence for POU5F1B.

grades_final.reason: E07 shows a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in HCT 116, but ChIP occupancy is not allele-specific; no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup for TCF7L2 is provided, so the alt-C-strengthens-binding claim is only indirectly consistent.

E01 and E03 directly place the variant in the pELS EH38E3858447, and E07 directly reports a TCF7L2 ENCODE ChIP-seq peak containing this region in HCT 116. This supports co-localization of variant, element, and TCF7L2 occupancy.

E02 gives MYC as 334.2 kb upstream and E06 includes general 8q24/MYC colorectal cancer literature, but there is no eQTL, reporter, CRISPR, or chromatin-interaction evidence directly linking this cCRE/variant to MYC. Distance and general literature are only indirect.
E07 supports TCF7L2 occupancy at this element in HCT 116, a colorectal cancer cell line, but the allele-specific TCF7L2 effect and downstream MYC effect are not demonstrated in HCT 116.

E06 provides only general colorectal cancer/MYC context. E04 reports no GWAS Catalog association for rs73706717, and E05 is for PSA and urinary incontinence, not colorectal cancer. No provided evidence ties rs73706717 to MYC expression or colorectal cancer risk.

E03 reports CTCF ChIP signal at the containing cCRE, but the values are maxima across ENCODE biosamples and are not allele-specific. No QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup for CTCF is provided. The claim that alt C strengthens CTCF binding is therefore only indirectly consistent, not shown.
E01 and E03 directly show the variant lies in the pELS EH38E3858447, and E03 directly reports CTCF ChIP signal at this cCRE. This supports the element/CTCF co-localization claim.

E02 places POU5F1B closest and in the gene body, and E05 gives POU5F1B the best L2G score, but those credible sets are for PSA and urinary incontinence with PIP 0.04, not colorectal cancer. No direct regulatory link from this variant/element to POU5F1B expression is provided.

E03 CTCF ChIP support is not HCT 116-specific, and E06 provides only general POU5F1B colorectal cancer literature. The proposed CTCF-mediated effect in colorectal cancer cells is not directly demonstrated.

E09 gives a gene-level POU5F1B-colorectal cancer Open Targets score of 0.54, and E06 gives general literature, but no variant-level evidence links rs73706717 to POU5F1B expression or colorectal cancer. Direction is also unresolved: if CTCF acts as an insulator, stronger alt-C CTCF binding would predict lower POU5F1B, but this is not tested and E04/E05 do not provide a colorectal cancer association.

E07 shows TCF7L2 ChIP-seq occupancy of an element containing the variant in HCT 116, but it does not establish allele-specific binding. No QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup for TCF7L2 is provided, so the alt-C-strengthens-TCF7L2 claim remains unsupported by direct allele-specific evidence.

E01 and E03 directly place the variant in pELS EH38E3858447, and E07 directly reports a TCF7L2 ENCODE ChIP-seq peak containing this region in HCT 116. This supports the element/TCF7L2 co-localization claim.

E02 places POU5F1B closest and in the gene body, and E05 gives it the best L2G score, but the credible sets are non-colorectal-cancer traits with PIP 0.04. No direct regulatory evidence connects this cCRE/variant to POU5F1B expression.
E07 supports TCF7L2 occupancy at this element in HCT 116, but the allele-specific TCF7L2 effect on POU5F1B is not demonstrated in HCT 116 or other colorectal cancer cells.

E09 gives a gene-level POU5F1B-colorectal cancer score of 0.54 and E06 gives general colorectal cancer literature, but no provided evidence ties rs73706717 to POU5F1B expression or to colorectal cancer risk. E04 shows no GWAS Catalog association for the variant.

checks.why: Tests whether the variant lies in a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak in the provided colorectal cancer cell context; absence would strongly weaken chain_2’s binding step.
